# VRFrameworkDebugMode

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · assembly `VRFramework.Core.Editors` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Editor/VRFrameworkDebugMode.cs#L16)

Debug Mode is the VRF_DEBUG scripting define and nothing else. One switch decides both what
the framework logs about itself (see Util.LogDebug) and which [DebugOnly] fields the
inspector shows, and because it is a define rather than a setting the verbose tier is not
merely skipped in a production build - it is not compiled into it.
The define is written for every build target the project can produce, so turning it on does
not quietly apply to the desktop player and miss the headset.

## Properties

### Enabled {#enabled}

Whether the editor is currently compiled with the define. Read from the symbol the editor
itself was built with rather than from player settings, so it cannot disagree with the
code that is actually running.

## Methods

### Set(bool) {#set-boolean}

Adds or removes the define, which triggers a recompile. Every target is visited even when
the first one already agrees, so a project whose targets have drifted apart is put back
in step rather than left half switched.
